topic: A Water Tower Uses Height to Push Water
creativeBrief:
Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Audience: global English-speaking viewers; state country, model and time scope naturally. Channel angle: familiar objects with a surprising but true job. Generate five declarative, concrete subject-first hooks; prefer 6–10 words and do not give away the mechanism at once. Six story functions across five voiced scenes: visual paradox, contradiction, clue, mechanism, distinct second reveal, payoff. Target 25–29 seconds including the configured sign-off; hard max 30. Keep voice, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. No generic spoken CTA. Visual direction: Use the photoreal live-action style in visualStyle, like varied Pexels-style footage. Open on the real object and its surprising visible detail. Build five distinct camera setups: vary at least two of shot scale, angle, location, lighting and physical action between neighboring scenes. Prefer observable actions, practical macro details, human hands, and real-world context over abstract visual metaphors. For a hidden mechanism, use a plausible exposed component or demonstration prop without pretending an invented event was filmed. Keep brand signs out if accurate rendering is doubtful. Generate a distinct Gemini still and Google Flow six-second clip per voiced scene; review action, 9:16 crop and continuity before binding local MP4s. Generated shots explain sourced facts and are not documentary proof. Packaging: make the YouTube title and description curiosity-driven, a little provocative, and specific to the subject; deliver exactly the claim the video explains. The title may tease the mechanism, but do not exaggerate risk, savings, universality or a company motive beyond the facts. The description should invite one topic-specific viewer response.
YouTube title seed: Why Your Water Tower Is So High
YouTube description seed: Once water is up in a tower, gravity can help move it through the pipes. Is there a water tower near you? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
Core fact: USGS explains that elevated water storage supplies distribution pressure.
Second reveal: Pumps can fill the tower, then gravity moves stored water through pipes.
Opening shot: a water tower above house taps. Show it as a believable real-world shot, immediately legible in the first frame. Do not reveal the internal mechanism in the opening. Use different real camera compositions and meaningful subject motion for the clue, mechanism, second reveal and payoff. Do not use an imaginary accident, simulated rescue, or fake news-style scene. 
Fact boundaries: Pressure also depends on system design and elevation; not all towns use towers.
